---
title: Claiming a listing
description: How a vendor proves they represent a tool, what the verification code does and does not do, and what a claim unlocks.
---

Claiming is how you establish that you work for the vendor. It unlocks
[listing edits](/docs/vendors/what-you-can-change),
[price proposals](/docs/vendors/correcting-a-price) and
[screenshot uploads](/docs/vendors/logos-and-screenshots) for that one tool.

Start from the tool's own page while signed in.

## What we ask for

**A work email address on the tool's own domain.** Not a personal one: an address at
Gmail, Outlook, Proton, iCloud, Yahoo and similar is never auto-matched, because anyone can
hold one and it says nothing about who employs you.

The domain check is a plain host comparison against the tool's homepage — so
`you@acme.com` matches a tool at `acme.com` or `docs.acme.com`. Vendor mail on a different
domain from the marketing site is common and does **not** fail your claim; it just routes
you to a person, which is where an ambiguous case belongs anyway. Use the evidence field to
say what the relationship is.

## The code

We email a six-digit code to the address you gave. It expires in **30 minutes**, and only
its hash is stored on our side.

The code confirms one thing: that you can receive mail at that address. **It is not a
sign-in code**, it cannot be used to access an account, and it does not by itself transfer
a listing. A code issued for one claim cannot be used to verify another, even one you filed
yourself.

## Review

**A person reviews every claim before any listing changes hands**, including claims where
the domain matched automatically. A verified email is evidence, not authority.

Once approved, the tool appears in [your listings](/my-listings).

## What a claim does not give you

It does not give you editorial control. You cannot change our description, our strengths
and limitations, the tool's slug, its sort order, or any benchmark score — and you cannot
write a price directly. See [what you can change](/docs/vendors/what-you-can-change) for
the exact line and the reasoning behind it.
